keywords: Ultimate Egypt Pharaohs Pyramids and a Nile Cruise

tagline: Sixteen cabins, a four-poster in each, and the river between Luxor and Aswan.
answer: Sun Boat III is a 16-cabin A&K Sanctuary riverboat on the Nile between Luxor and Aswan, built in a 1920s Golden Age style with a four-poster bed in every cabin. She takes 32 guests and children from 10. A&K sells her as a private charter or as a seven-night Luxor to Aswan cruise inside its 13-day Ultimate Egypt journey. She suits couples and small groups.

overview: Sun Boat III looks like a superyacht from the riverbank and like the 1920s inside. A&K built the interiors around the Golden Age of Nile travel: brass, teak, ecru fabrics, a spiral staircase, vintage gramophones and a four-poster in every cabin. Architectural Digest called her the "Jewel of the Nile", and A&K repeats it.

There are 16 cabins and suites for 32 guests. The bar is named for Howard Carter, the shelves carry archaeology books, and the sun deck has a plunge pool, palms and gazebos for shade. Days ashore run with an Egyptologist: Karnak, Luxor Temple, the Valley of the Kings, Edfu, Kom Ombo and Philae.

A&K does not publish a cruise-only fare for her. She is sold as a private charter, priced on enquiry, or as the seven-night river section of Ultimate Egypt: Pharaohs, Pyramids and a Nile Cruise, which adds Cairo and a flight to Abu Simbel.
why: We put people on Sun Boat III when the boat matters as much as the temples. Sixteen cabins means a small dining room and a quiet sun deck, and the period interiors are the point, not a theme. For a family or a group of friends who want the whole boat, she is the charter we look at first. For two travellers, the Ultimate Egypt departures give seven nights on board rather than the usual four.

days.title: Karnak and Luxor Temple
days.summary: Fly from Cairo and visit the Temple of Karnak before boarding for lunch. Afternoon at the Temple of Luxor, then a welcome cocktail and dinner.

days.title: The Valley of the Kings
days.summary: West Bank day: the Colossi of Memnon, the Temple of Hatshepsut and the Valley of the Kings, including Tutankhamun, Ramses VI and Seti I, plus Howard Carter's house. Later, the Luxor Museum.

days.title: Balloon at dawn, Medinet Habu
days.summary: An early hot-air balloon flight over the temples, then Medinet Habu and a visit to Funtasia Children's School, subject to the school calendar. Cruise toward Esna.

days.title: Esna and Edfu
days.summary: The Temple of Khnum at Esna with your Egyptologist, then on to Edfu for the Temple of Horus.

days.title: Kom Ombo
days.summary: A morning on board with a cooking session led by the chef. Walk to the Temple of Kom Ombo, then a galabeya night with an Egyptian buffet and music.

days.title: Aswan and Philae
days.summary: The granite quarries and the Unfinished Obelisk, then by boat to Philae on Agilika Island and the Nubian Museum. A felucca sail around Elephantine Island, weather permitting.

days.title: Abu Simbel
days.summary: Fly to Abu Simbel for the temple of Ramses II, lunch, and fly back to Aswan.

days.title: Disembark in Aswan
days.summary: Leave the boat and fly to Cairo, where the journey continues.

faqs: How many cabins does Sun Boat III have?
16: twelve Luxury Cabins, two Presidential Suites and two Royal Suites, for up to 32 guests. Every cabin has a four-poster bed.
Where does Sun Boat III sail?
The Nile between Luxor and Aswan. On A&K's Ultimate Egypt journey she sails seven nights from Luxor to Aswan, with Esna, Edfu, Kom Ombo and a flight to Abu Simbel along the way.
Can you book Sun Boat III as a cruise only?
A&K does not publish a cruise-only fare. She is sold as a private charter, priced on enquiry, or inside the 13-day Ultimate Egypt: Pharaohs, Pyramids and a Nile Cruise journey.
Can I charter the whole of Sun Boat III?
Yes. A&K describes her as a charter boat whose itinerary can be shaped to the group. With 16 cabins she suits a family gathering or friends travelling together.
Is Sun Boat III suitable for children?
Children aged 10 and over are welcome, and under-15s share a cabin with an adult. Younger children are not accepted.
Which Sun Boat III cabin should I book?

The Luxury Cabins (16 sq m) have showers. The Presidential Suites (28 sq m) add a lounge and bathtub. The two Royal Suites (39 sq m) sit alone on the Tower Deck with private balconies; book those early.
What is the difference between Sun Boat III and Sun Boat IV?
Sun Boat III has 16 cabins and a 1920s interior with four-posters throughout. Sun Boat IV has 38 cabins, a larger pool deck and a massage room, and sells as a regular four-night cruise.
All meals, water, tea and coffee at meals, juices at breakfast, afternoon tea, and guided excursions with entrance fees. Drinks, gratuities and laundry are extra.
